verdict.justification: Both deliverables correctly prioritize the approved 21-day notice over the unapproved 84-day proposal and clearly identify outstanding approvals. B provides the more executable continuity strategy, translating demand into a 4,200–5,400-set last-time buy and explaining how moulding ahead permits tooling transfer while LPI finishes electronics and assembly. Its dated transition gates, escalation triggers, and explicit units-versus-sets check make the plan more useful in executive negotiations. A materially miscalculates the electronics development dates: four to five months from 23 October is approximately February–March, not its stated March–April, and its action plan further delays kickoff without consistently updating those dates. A also weakens its BATNA by including an LPI pre-build and relying on an extension, whereas B distinguishes the no-bridge alternative and quantifies the resulting production exposure. B's proposed bridge remains conditional on ramp-up, moulding capacity, approvals, and stock verification, but it identifies those dependencies rather than presenting them as secured commitments.

decisive_issues.issue: Electronics readiness dates overstate the stated four-to-five-month development duration by approximately one month.
The BATNA depends partly on cooperation and an extension from the counterparty rather than cleanly separating the no-agreement contingency.
decisive_issues.quote: Hence the BATNA is only as strong as the buffer and extension we can secure

decisive_issues.issue: Provides a concrete tooling-release mechanism that preserves LPI assembly while enabling local development.
decisive_issues.quote: LPI moulds the plastic components for the full LTB in the first four weeks, then releases the tools on Day 28 (20 Nov 2026) while it continues electronics and final assembly to Day 84.

decisive_issues.issue: Explicitly flags a material capacity-unit ambiguity and defines an early escalation rule.
decisive_issues.quote: If LPI's 1,500/2,500 capacity means individual lamps and not sets, the 4,200-set floor needs 8,400 lamps, which exceeds 84 days at 2,500 lamps/month (≈7,000). Recompute and escalate by Day 3.
